tcmateditor.title: Tinkers' Material Editor
tcmateditor.label.name: Name
tcmateditor.page.general.hint: Basic settings and the items used to make this material.
tcmateditor.page.stats.hint: Switch a part type on to allow building it from this material. Changes apply automatically.
tcmateditor.page.traits.hint: Traits are the built-in entries of a material. Default traits apply to every part, groups can override them.
tcmateditor.section.material_slots.hint: Tools made with this material gain or lose slots. Counts once, no matter how many parts use it.
tcmateditor.page.texture.hint: Part textures are greyscale sprites colored by the palette, then layered with effects. Press Apply to update in game.
tcmateditor.page.info.hint: Name and description go into language files and show in tooltips and the Tinkers' books.
tcmateditor.page.entry.hint: An entry is a custom bonus. Each line changes one value, modifier slot or potion effect and can scale with level. Add it to a material on its Traits tab.
tcmateditor.page.entry_info.hint: Name and description of the entry.
tcmateditor.section.items.hint: Put these items in the Part Builder to get the material. Value = material given, Needed = items used.
tcmateditor.section.ingame.not_loaded: Press Apply to see the real in game items here.
tcmateditor.section.stat_traits.hint: Traits for a single part type (like helmet plating). These take priority.
tcmateditor.section.palette.hint: Dark on the left, light on the right. Drag stops to move, click the bar to add, right click to remove.
tcmateditor.section.effects.hint: Applied top to bottom. Region limits an effect to shadows, midtones, highlights or edges.
tcmateditor.section.usage.none: No material uses this entry yet.
tcmateditor.hint.number: Range %s to %s, scroll to adjust (Shift x10)
tcmateditor.hint.material_id: namespace:name using lowercase letters, digits and _. Using an existing material ID overrides it.
tcmateditor.hint.tier: Used for sorting and display, not mining level
tcmateditor.hint.craftable: When off the material can only be cast
tcmateditor.hint.hidden: Hidden from the books and JEI
tcmateditor.hint.add_held: Add the item in your main hand
tcmateditor.hint.fluid: Melts in the smeltery and parts can be cast from it
tcmateditor.hint.fluid_id: Must be a fluid ID such as tconstruct:molten_iron, not an item
tcmateditor.hint.give_test: Get a pickaxe, sword, longbow and chestplate made from this material (creative or operator)
tcmateditor.hint.statless: This part has no numbers, just switch it on
tcmateditor.hint.own_traits: When off the default traits are used
tcmateditor.hint.generate_palette: Builds shades automatically from the chosen color
tcmateditor.hint.base_style: Greyscale sprite set to start from (metal, wood, rock…)
tcmateditor.hint.open_patterns: Put PNG files in this folder to use them with the Pattern effect
tcmateditor.hint.animation: Creates animated textures, they keep working after export
tcmateditor.hint.animation_armor: Worn armor textures cannot animate and use the first frame.
tcmateditor.hint.editing_language: Editing the %s texts, switch the language with ? at the top right. Empty languages use the text of another language.
tcmateditor.hint.desc: What makes the material special, shown in the books
tcmateditor.hint.follow_texture: Turn off to pick your own color
tcmateditor.hint.kind: Tool stat = Tinkers' tool value; Attribute = player attribute (speed, health…); Slots = add or remove modifier slots; Effect = potion effect on hit or when hit
tcmateditor.hint.slot_line: Adds modifier slots to the tool, negative numbers remove them. Whole numbers only.
tcmateditor.hint.effect_line: Applies a potion effect when attacking, when hit, or when using the tool
tcmateditor.hint.export: Export a mod jar, or a data pack plus resource pack, that work without this mod
tcmateditor.hint.auto_apply: Reload data automatically after edits (off by default). Textures and texts still need Apply.
tcmateditor.hint.namespace: Namespace for new materials and entries
tcmateditor.hint.ui_language: Language of the editor, the Info tab also edits texts in this language
tcmateditor.empty.upgrades: No upgrades yet. Upgrades put entries onto equipment in the Tinker Station or Tinkers' Anvil.
tcmateditor.page.upgrade.hint: An upgrade adds an entry to equipment in the Tinker Station or Tinkers' Anvil: equipment in the middle, materials in their slots.
tcmateditor.page.upgrade_tools.hint: Choose which equipment can take this upgrade. The deny list wins over the allow list.
tcmateditor.hint.anvil_only: This slot only exists on the Tinkers' Anvil, not the Tinker Station.
tcmateditor.hint.slot_type: Which modifier slot the upgrade consumes
tcmateditor.hint.max_level: Highest level it can be stacked to
tcmateditor.hint.allow_crystal: Allows re-applying with a Tinkers' modifier crystal
tcmateditor.hint.strict_slots: When on, each material must be in its own slot
tcmateditor.hint.strict_on: Exact slots: each material must be in its slot. Without this mod the recipe falls back to any order and still works.
tcmateditor.hint.strict_off: Any order: materials can go in any slot (plain Tinkers' recipe).
tcmateditor.hint.add_tool_ref: Add a specific item or item tag
tcmateditor.hint.make_upgrade: Create an upgrade recipe for this entry
tcmateditor.section.anvil.hint: Click a slot, then set its material. Right click clears. Hover the ? for slot numbers.
tcmateditor.section.deny_tools.hint: These can never take the upgrade, even if allowed above.
tcmateditor.section.tools_preview: Tinkers' equipment that can use it
tcmateditor.section.tools_preview.count: %s of %s Tinkers' items can use it
tcmateditor.warn.no_inputs: Add at least one material, otherwise no recipe is created.
tcmateditor.warn.no_tools: Nothing selected means every Tinkers' item can use it.
tcmateditor.help.anvil_note: Numbered clockwise starting from the lapis slot. The Tinker Station only has slots 1, 4 and 5; slots 2 and 3 exist only on the anvil.
tcmateditor.help.8: Upgrades turn entries into Tinker Station / Anvil recipes, with a material per slot and a list of allowed equipment.
tcmateditor.picker.import: Pick a material to use as template
tcmateditor.field.durability.hint: Head and similar: actual durability. Handle and grip: percent bonus
tcmateditor.field.mining_speed.hint: Head: base speed. Handle: percent bonus
tcmateditor.field.melee_damage.hint: Handle: percent bonus. Grip: flat bonus
tcmateditor.effect.noise.hint: Random light and dark grain, good for stone and ores
tcmateditor.effect.sparkle.hint: Random bright dots, good for gems
tcmateditor.effect.gradient.hint: Fades to the chosen color from handle to tip
tcmateditor.effect.pattern.hint: Overlays an image (a block texture or your own PNG)
tcmateditor.trigger.weapon.hint: Melee or projectile hit, the target gets it (melee needs a full swing)
tcmateditor.trigger.counter.hint: Armor: whoever attacks you gets it, uses 1 durability each time
tcmateditor.trigger.armor_attack.hint: Armor: anything you hit with any weapon while wearing it
tcmateditor.trigger.self.hint: You get it when mining, attacking or shooting with the tool
tcmateditor.op.add.hint: Adds the value, negative values reduce
tcmateditor.op.multiply_base.hint: Multiplies the base value by (1 + value)
tcmateditor.op.multiply_conditional.hint: Multiplies by (1 + value) without showing in tool stats
tcmateditor.slot.head: Head
tcmateditor.empty.materials: No materials yet. Create one, or import an existing material as a template.
tcmateditor.empty.entries: No entries yet. Entries are custom bonuses you can give to materials.
tcmateditor.dialog.delete.title: Delete "%s"?
tcmateditor.dialog.delete.message: It is removed from the game the next time you apply.
tcmateditor.help.title: How it works
tcmateditor.help.1: Shift+Z opens the editor, Ctrl+S saves, Ctrl+Shift+S saves and reloads.
tcmateditor.help.2: Apply saves and hot reloads: stats change instantly, textures and names refresh the resources.
tcmateditor.help.3: Import uses an existing material as a template you can change freely.
tcmateditor.help.4: Entries are custom bonuses, like +2 damage and -10% attack speed. Add them on a material's Traits tab.
tcmateditor.help.5: Textures: drag the palette to recolor, add effects and animation. Put your own PNGs in the pattern folder.
tcmateditor.help.6: Export creates a mod jar (just drop it into mods) and a data pack plus resource pack, all in plain Tinkers' format. They work without this mod.
tcmateditor.help.7: In multiplayer the server needs this mod too, and you must be an operator.
tcmateditor.status.saved: Saved (not in a world, nothing to reload)
tcmateditor.status.saved_only: Saved (not reloaded, Ctrl+Shift+S saves and reloads)
tcmateditor.status.no_server: The server does not have this mod: saved, use Export instead
tcmateditor.status.nothing_given: No tool can use this material yet
tcmateditor.status.unknown_material: Material %s is not in the game yet, apply first
tcmateditor.status.shortcuts: Ctrl+S save · Ctrl+Shift+S save and reload
tcmateditor.export.title: Exported (use one of the two options)
tcmateditor.export.jar: Recommended: put %s into the mods folder (client and server). One file holds everything.
tcmateditor.export.packs: Or: put %s into <world>/datapacks and %s into resourcepacks, then enable it under Resource Packs. The resource pack does nothing inside datapacks.
tcmateditor.export.problems: %s references do not exist in this game and were left out:
tcmateditor.problem.slots_id_taken: the slot trait ID %s is already used by an entry
tcmateditor.status.applied_with_problems: Applied %s files, left out %s invalid references: %s
tcmateditor.status.data_pending: ● Unapplied changes, press Apply or Ctrl+Shift+S
